question: Why does the in-guest LiteInst flagship fail the authoritative liteinst_strict_verify_virtual_identity_and_time gate (date +%s returns host wall-clock instead of the deterministic epoch)?
answer: RESOLVED (runtime-instrumented): the in-guest Tool determinizes the raw clock_gettime syscall (raw=epoch) but the glibc vDSO fast path leaks host wall-clock (vdso=host) because at the pinned 456b628 reverie-liteinst backend.rs launch() runs the guest via a plain std::process::Command::spawn() (line 620) with NO TracerBuilder/ptrace supervisor, so vdso_patch (only reachable via ptrace tracee_preinit at task.rs:1757) never runs. LiteInst's only interceptor is reverie-preload InProcessSeccomp, which traps syscall INSTRUCTIONS; the vDSO fast path issues no syscall instruction so is never trapped. OWNER-GATED, NOT a contained fix: remedy = HybridPtrace lifecycle controller (lifecycle.rs:82-104 skeleton returns Unsupported) that reaches post-exec preinit and calls the existing vdso_patch, or in-guest vDSO self-patch (fail-closed EOPNOTSUPP, glibc-version-dependent). Both change the LiteInst interception/lifecycle mechanism -> Reverie API Policy owner-gate. Correction: earlier 'bounded, not owner-gated' framing was WRONG (it assumed a TracerBuilder::<()> supervisor, which is the later 8c9aad1/#337 commit, not 456b628).
key_source: reverie-ptrace/src/vdso.rs:247 vdso_patch (rewrites __vdso_clock_gettime etc to mov+syscall+ret stubs)
reverie-ptrace/src/task.rs:1757 vdso_patch called UNGATED in tracee_preinit
reverie-preload/src/seccomp.rs for_trusted_gate: traps every syscall by IP except trusted gate; vDSO fast path makes NO syscall so is uncovered unless vdso_patch redirects it
